components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: linear-gradient(to right, #7c5cfc, #6947e0); color: #f4f2fb; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; padding: 16px 48px; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), box-shadow 150ms ease; box-shadow: 0 0 40px rgba(124,92,252,0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: scale(1.02); box-shadow: 0 0 50px rgba(124,92,252,0.65); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #22d3ee; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; transform: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Secondary CTA. Transparent background, border, cyan hover state.

narrative.overview:
Chord Map exists in abstract harmonic space — a dark void where chord relationships become visible geometry. Nodes float like celestial bodies; transitions glow like gravitational pulls. The design draws from astronomical visualization: controlled darkness punctuated by precise, luminous accents. This is not a music production tool or a music notation app. It is a map, and maps work best when the terrain is legible against the background.

The palette is built on two forces: gravity (violet — the tonic, home, resolution) and tension (cyan — the dominant, movement, energy). Amber, rose, and mint appear as tertiary signals — genre context, alerts, success states — but never compete with the primary axis. The dark ink background is not just aesthetic; it is the canvas on which the graph becomes legible.

Key characteristics: Dark cosmic void with controlled luminous accents; Violet as gravity/home, cyan as tension/movement; Generative Three.js hero sets the creative tone while functional pages stay focused; Tonal layering instead of shadows; Typography mixes Space Grotesk (geometric confidence) with Inter (readable body) and JetBrains Mono (technical labels).
keyCharacteristics: Dark cosmic void with controlled luminous accents
Violet as gravity/home, cyan as tension/movement
Generative Three.js hero sets the creative tone; functional pages stay focused
Tonal layering instead of shadows — no depth on flat surfaces
Space Grotesk for headings, Inter for body, JetBrains Mono for technical labels

rules.name: The Gravity Rule
rules.body: Violet appears where the user should feel settled — home chords, primary actions, active states. Its use is earned, not ambient.

rules.name: The Tension Rule
rules.body: Cyan appears where there is forward motion — secondary actions, hover states, data accents. It never dominates a full surface; it highlights what moves.

rules.name: The One-Tenth Rule
rules.body: Cyan, amber, rose, and mint together occupy ≤10% of any given screen. Their rarity is the point — when they appear, they signal something specific.

rules.name: The Mono Label Rule
rules.body: Chord symbols, Roman numerals, and musical notation always use JetBrains Mono. Mixing serif or sans-serif for musical notation breaks the technical precision the tool projects.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. The only shadow behavior is the glow effect on primary buttons, which is luminosity, not depth.

dos: Do use violet as the primary action color — it signals home, resolution, primary flow
Do use cyan for secondary actions and hover states on non-primary elements
Do keep functional pages focused — the Three.js hero is for the landing page only
Do use JetBrains Mono for all musical notation (Roman numerals, chord symbols, genre keys)
Do use tonal layering for depth — surface-hi on hover, surface for resting state
Do use the full rounded button shape — it signals approachability
Do maintain WCAG A contrast ratios
donts: Don't use violet or cyan as decorative fills on non-interactive elements
Don't add shadows — tonal layering IS the depth system
Don't use border-left or border-right as colored accent stripes
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text) for headings
Don't repeat the hero's Three.js canvas on sub-pages
Don't use Press Start 2P for functional UI text
Don't create card grids with identical patterns throughout
Don't use generic AI-generated UI patterns
